name: Constructivist photomontage poster
summary: Cut-out photographs are pasted with drawn shapes and big type, then copied by photo-lithography or by halftone blocks in two to four flat inks. The diagonals, the red and black blocks and the sans-serif capitals come from the montage and the spot colour.

philosophy.core_thesis: A poster made of real photographs, set on strong diagonals and printed in a few hard colours, speaks as a fact and not as a picture.
design_principles: Cut each photograph to a hard edge and paste it on the layout; do not feather or blend it.
Set the main axis on a diagonal of 15–45° and let the figures lean along it.
Change the scale of the photographs sharply: a face as large as the sheet beside a crowd as small as a thumb.
Use 2–4 flat inks: red, black, cream paper and, in some sheets, ochre. Put the red in blocks and wedges.
Make the photographs with a coarse halftone of 50–80 lines an inch so that they print on cheap paper.
Set the slogan in heavy sans-serif capitals, in red or black, and give it a block of its own.
Use geometric shapes (circle, bar, wedge) as frames and as pointers, and leave no ornament.
anti_patterns: Soft blends and drop shadows between photographs
A centred, symmetrical layout with no diagonal
Ornament, script type and floral borders
A fine halftone that looks like a photograph in a magazine

process.matrix: A photo-lithographic plate or a zinc halftone block, made from the pasted montage.
process.press: A flatbed lithographic press or a letterpress machine at a state printing house.
process.image_making: The designer cuts photographs and paper shapes and pastes them on a board. A camera copies the montage through a screen, and the colour plates are drawn by hand.
process.edition: Thousands of sheets, all the same; the print is a machine copy of a hand-made master.

inks.strategy: Opaque spot inks: a red for the blocks, a black for the photographs and the type, and sometimes an ochre, on a cream sheet.

colours.name: Black
colours.role: the photo tone and the type

screening.rule: Screen each photograph at a coarse 50–80 lines an inch; the dots show at reading distance.

registration.rule: The plates register within 1 mm. A small gap between the red block and the black photograph is normal.

substrate.stock: A machine-made paper, cream or light grey, uncoated or with a light coat.
substrate.finish: Matt and smooth, with a slight tooth; the paper yellows with age.

surface.impression: No bite; a flat lithographic film of ink on the surface.
surface.sheen: Matt, with a slight sheen in the red solids.
surface.texture: Coarse halftone dots, hard cut edges of photographs and a faint grain in the large solids.

evidence.title: Under the banner of Lenin for socialist construction

emotion.target_response: Hard, confident drive: the viewer feels a call to act, in a layout that leans forward and uses real faces.

avoid_when: The message must feel soft, calm or luxurious.
The design uses no photographs and no strong diagonal.

modifiers.how: Replace the photographs with a painted figure in a thick black contour; keep the red, the black and the heavy caption.
Change the photographic halftone for coarse flat dot tints; keep the flat red and black.
